That completes checking the tricky situations across every part of the app — saving, finding, read-later, archiving, editing, and the empty/overflow states all hold up. I don't see time-based behavior this app needs (nothing expires or changes by date beyond your chosen sort order), so I believe the picture is complete.

Here's everything that's settled, in plain terms:

- **Saving a link:** paste an address (with or without `https://`), the app fills in the title, description, site icon, and a preview image automatically, and you can edit any of it. It handles a mistyped address gracefully and still lets you save by hand when a page's details can't be read.
- **Tags & notes:** add your own tags — with suggestions from tags you already use — plus a personal note.
- **Finding things:** search across everything (title, description, site, address, tags, notes), filter by clicking a tag, and sort by newest, oldest, or title.
- **Read later:** flag links into a focused Read-later list and clear them when done.
- **Archiving:** tuck links away to keep your main list uncluttered, and restore them anytime.
- **Editing & no duplicates:** edit any saved bookmark (including its address), and the app prevents duplicate links — sending you to the existing one instead, wherever it lives.
- **Holds up when empty or overloaded:** a welcoming first-run screen, and tidy wrapping for very long text and many tags.

That's **12 settled behaviors**, all just for you and kept in one private place.

**May I now go ahead and build this scope as the real application?** Once you approve, I'll switch from exploring to actually implementing it. (Anything new you think of after that, I'll note for a later round rather than expanding this build.)
